mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue rising from their recent troughs, weekday trip chaining will improve and retail visits will recover over the next four weeks. This mechanism predicts higher RETAIL_REC because more commuters create more incidental shopping stops near stations and offices.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next 28 days despite a continued 2-week rise in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: A further decline in RESIDENTIAL time indicates more out-of-home activity and weaker stay-at-home substitution, which should lift RETAIL_REC within one week by freeing discretionary shopping time.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 7 days after RESIDENTIAL falls relative to its prior week.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT improves by at least 3 points week-on-week from an already depressed level, access friction falls enough to raise retail-and-recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 3 points week-on-week after being below -35
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 14 days after TRANSIT crosses the stated improvement threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A combined rise in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS signals broader out-of-home mobility and trip clustering, which spills over into retail visits over the next four weeks. The effect should be stronger when both series rise together than when only one improves.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days in periods where both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS increase together.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility rebounds first, it usually marks favorable weather and more weekend outing demand, which then spills into retail and recreation spending within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above its prior 2-week average by at least 5 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after PARKS exceeds its 2-week average by the stated margin.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while WORKPLACES stays depressed, people are still substituting home-based routines for discretionary shopping, so RETAIL_REC will remain lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying above baseline and WORKPLACES staying below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in WORKPLACES over two consecutive weeks should strengthen weekday demand around business districts and raise RETAIL_REC, but only after commuting has stabilized rather than bouncing for a single week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not outperform its prior 4-week mean after WORKPLACES rises for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and GROCERY_PHARM both weaken together, it indicates fewer linked trips and reduced circulation, which should pull RETAIL_REC lower within one week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 7 days after both TRANSIT and GROCERY_PHARM fall together.
